messages:
sam-peopleops: Heads up  Lena has an IC (Omar) approved for a band move effective 2026-12-01. Recruiting is also about to extend an external offer with matching comp for parity. Lena asked if we should retro to 12/01 so the internal comp matches the offer, or make it 12/15 and add a signing adjustment for parity.
lena-engmgr: We want parity with the offer we plan to send tomorrow. If we do retro, will that complicate the candidate offer / start date paperwork?
recruiting-biz: If you want comps aligned immediately, easiest is to confirm internal comp effective date 12/01. If payroll can't hit 12/15 with retro, we can include a one-time sign-on credit in the offer that mirrors the retro amount. Which approach reduces admin?
omar-ic: I'm in EMEA, any different rules for retro or sign-on payments there? Also will this affect my benefits enrollment window?
sam-peopleops: Short answer: retro is doable but depends on payroll cutoff and approvals. Sign-on adjustment is simpler from a payroll perspective if deadlines are tight. Benefits: if effective date is 12/01, benefits eligibility typically follows the plan rules (often start of the month). For EMEA, local payroll may need extra lead time for compliance/tax accounting.
lena-engmgr: What approvals do we need to do retro? I have manager + director notes. Is HR approval enough?
sam-peopleops: You need: manager+director approval, completed comp-change form in Workday flagged "retro", attach calibration note, and email hr-escalations CC payroll and recruiting. For cross-border folks include local compensation approval from People Ops EMEA.
recruiting-biz: If you pick the sign-on route we can bake the one-time payment into the offer letter now and avoid retro complexity; payroll will record it as a bonus-like payment. Note: sign-on bonuses are taxed differently in some countries and may affect bonus target calculations.
payroll-bot: Payroll cutoff FYI: to hit 2026-12-15 run changes must be approved in Workday by 2026-12-10 23:59 PT. International changes often require a 5 business day buffer before that. Sign-on payments can be scheduled in the next run if necessary but may carry different tax handling.
omar-ic: If we do retro to 12/01 and it lands on 12/15, will the retro be shown separately on my paystub? And how is holiday pay treated if retro overlaps a company holiday?
sam-peopleops: Retro shows as separate earning lines on the paystub with the retro date range. Holiday pay is paid per company policy; if retro increases your rate and holiday accruals are tied to rate, payroll will recompute holiday-related payments for paid holiday days in the retro period. We'll note the specifics when payroll reviews the case.
lena-engmgr: Any interaction with a new hire sign-on if the internal person accepts the offer as well? We might shift org headcount.
recruiting-biz: If Omar stays and we cancel an external offer, recruiting will cancel the offer but we still need to reconcile any offer letters already sent. If the external candidate was already given an advance/relocation payment, that's separate and must be handled case-by-case.
sam-peopleops: Practical checklist if you want retro: 1) attach manager+director approval emails (PDF) 2) attach calibration excerpt or leveling rubric (PDF) 3) complete Workday comp-change with note "retro pay requested 2026-12-01 through 2026-12-14" 4) include local People Ops approver for EMEA 5) email hr-escalations CC payroll + recruiting. If any deadlines are missed, use sign-on adjustment instead.
payroll-bot: Reminder: PDFs only. Non-PDF attachments delay processing. For international cases include local tax ID and employment contract copy.
omar-ic: Thanks  I prefer retro if it doesn't block recruiting. If sign-on is cleaner we can go that route.
lena-engmgr: I'll gather approvals now and aim for the 12/10 cutoff. If we miss it we'll coordinate a sign-on line in the external offer instead.
sam-peopleops: Great. If you want sample Workday note, ping me and I'll paste one to copy/paste.
